tests.business_summary: Producer actor_a POST /api/articles/community-gardening-tips/comments; observer actor_a GET /api/articles/community-gardening-tips/comments; business predicate P14 requires producer_response $.comment (object) to be added between before $.comments (array) and after $.comments (array) by strict-tuple identity [$.id->$.id].

rationale_sources.raw_rationale: Proposed C01 lifecycle increment, not proven causality: the center write r20260901-190305-64cb:request:7 is POST /api/articles/community-gardening-tips/comments (201) whose prepared body carries $.comment.body, and its response shape exposes $.comment.id. The nearest same-actor/session comparable read before the center (request:4) and the fresh read after the center (request:8) are both GET /api/articles/community-gardening-tips/comments (200) exposing the array $.comments. ui-diff-0002 records 'There are no comments yet...' being replaced by a comment element. P14 added with a strict-tuple identity on the comment id is a proposed rule over these recorded reads; the recorded order alone does not establish that the center request caused the addition. Business setup workflow-action-0005 (article creation) is the only eligible setup action for request:7 and its created article path prefix matches the comment endpoint; setup is replayed before the before-read.

The center write's own response carries the created comment object at $.comment (shape includes $.comment.id integer, $.comment.body, $.comment.createdAt), and the fresh post-state read request:8 returns $.comments[*] members with the same member-relative field $.id. Comparing the pre-state collection $.comments (request:4) with the post-state collection $.comments (request:8) therefore proposes that this exact member was added, identified by the strict tuple on $.id; the UI diff also records one comment text appearing. Identity is frozen from the observed response shapes only.

The before GET comments (request:4) returned an empty comments array; the POST comment (request:7) created a comment (response $.comment with id); the after GET comments (request:8) contains one more comment matching the created comment's id. Grounded as a collection increase via P14 added.
